Hi Jared / Priya — great to meet today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap:
- Enterprise requirements we heard: company-wide SSO via Okta (SAML 2.0), customer-managed KMS (AWS CMK with HSM), and 5+ years of logging retention with SIEM export (splunk/QRadar).
- Primary constraint: data residency and auditability — looks like Private VPC or Dedicated with strong networking/KMS controls are the likely candidates (Hosted API likely won't meet the KMS/SSO/VPC ask).

Open questions / asks for your security/team: 
1) SSO: can you share your Okta metadata (IdP SAML XML) and whether you require IdP-initiated only or both?
2) KMS/HSM: will your security team require an on-prem HSM or is a customer-managed AWS KMS CMK with CloudHSM-backed keys acceptable?
3) Logging: exact retention window (you mentioned ~5 years) and whether logs must stay in your account or we can ship to your SIEM via secure forwarder.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- You share Okta metadata + security contact for KMS details (Jared?).
- We (Redwood) provide a short doc comparing Dedicated vs Private for your constraints and a high-level MAP (timeline and owners). (Attached: SSO-Integration-Checklist.pdf, private-vs-dedicated-compare.pdf)
- Schedule a 30-min technical call next week with your infra/security and our SEs to confirm feasibility and timeline.

I attached a short checklist and a comparison doc; Connor included here to weigh in on anything security-specific.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — recap looks right. Quick answers from our side: 

SSO:
- We use Okta, SAML 2.0. We need SP-initiated but can support IdP-initiated if required. I'll pull the metadata and send it to you by EOD tomorrow.

KMS/HSM:
- Our policy requires customer-managed keys. AWS KMS CMK backed by CloudHSM is acceptable; we do not want keys managed by a third party. Keys must be created in our AWS account and we need the ability to audit key usage.

Logging:
- Retention requirement: minimum 5 years. Logs must be archived in our S3 with restricted access. We also need real-time forwarding into Splunk for incident detection.

Networking / residency:
- All inference traffic must originate from our VPC or over a private connection; public hosted endpoints are a non-starter for our production workload.

Question: does Redwood Dedicated support VPC-only access and customer-managed KMS in a way that keeps keys in our account, or would we need Redwood Private for that? Also, timeline & ballpark pricing for a Private deployment vs Dedicated reserved pool would help for our internal planning.

I can loop in our infra lead if you want a technical deep-dive.

—Jared

Hi Jared — Dylan here (SE). Short answers and options so you have a clearer picture before the infra call: 

1) Hosted API: doesn't meet the KMS/VPC requirement because keys would be Redwood-managed and endpoints public. Not recommended for production given your asks.

2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): can be configured with private connectivity (VPC peering / AWS PrivateLink) in many cases; however, customer-managed KMS where the CMK lives in your AWS account is only supported on our Private deployment today in the strictest interpretation. We have a few enterprise Dedicated customers that use cross-account KMS wraps + strict audit hooks, but that requires additional network/ops controls and an architecture review. If auditability and key ownership in your account are hard requirements, Private is the safest path.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full control — KMS keys in your account, direct VPC placement, SIEM ingestion into your Splunk, and longer log retention policy. Longer lead time and different commercial model (platform fee + infra).

Suggested immediate next steps:
- Technical sync (30 min) to confirm whether a Dedicated architecture with cross-account KMS and PrivateLink could satisfy your auditors, or if Private is necessary.
- I'll prep a short options spreadsheet (cost / lead time / tradeoffs) for the call.

Link: https://docs.redwood.in/enterprise-private-vs-dedicated (see section "KMS and Networking")

Connor, anything to add from a compliance perspective?

Thanks,
